dialect.detail: Likely JMA ORCA or similar Japanese medical/business web-COBOL framework using MONFUNC, MCPAREA, SPAAREA, LINKAREA, SCRAREA conventions; SCR-HTTP-METHOD and SCR-HTTP-STATUS suggest a web/HTTP-oriented COBOL runtime (possibly Fujitsu NetCOBOL or similar Japanese vendor framework)

purpose.domain_detail: Web-oriented COBOL application using HTTP method dispatch (GET/POST) with database fetch operations via a proprietary MONFUNC interface; likely part of a Japanese business web-COBOL framework
purpose.summary: This program dispatches on HTTP method (GET or POST) received via a screen/linkage area. On GET, it opens a message context, selects rows from 'tbl_fetch_test', fetches them in a loop writing to a 'ma' table, then closes and returns the result in SCR-BODY. On POST, it returns a 404 status.

notable_features: HTTP method dispatch via EVALUATE SCR-HTTP-METHOD
Proprietary MONFUNC call interface for DB operations (MSGOPEN, DBSELECT, DBFETCH, MSGWRITE, MSGCLOSE)
7 COPY statements for DB and linkage areas
PERFORM UNTIL loop for fetch iteration
BINARY PIC S9(9) for return code
SCR-HTTP-STATUS and SCR-BODY suggest web/HTTP response handling
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS - uses proprietary DB abstraction
verdict.notes: The MONFUNC/MCPAREA/SCRAREA pattern is characteristic of Japanese web-COBOL frameworks (possibly JMA ORCA medical system or Fujitsu NetCOBOL web framework). Dialect confidence is medium because the specific vendor cannot be confirmed without seeing the copybooks. The program is a test/demo program (PROGRAM-ID TEST1) but has production-like structure.
